A.text: A particle of mass m and charge q has an initial velocity vector v = v_0 vector j. If an electric field vector E = E_0 vector i and magnetic field vector B = B_0 vector i act on the particle, its speed will double after a time:
A.sol_text:
Vector v = v_0 vector j (initial velocity in y-direction)
vector E = E_0 vector i (electric field in x-direction)
vector B = B_0 vector i (magnetic field in x-direction)

Force on particle: vector F = q(vector E + vector v × vector B)

Since vector v × vector B:
Vector v × vector B = v_0 vector j × B_0 vector i = -v_0 B_0 vector k

Electric force: F_E = qE_0 vector i (in x-direction)
Magnetic force: F_B = -qv_0 B_0 vector k (in z-direction)

Acceleration in x-direction: a_x = qE_0/m
No force in y-direction initially: a_y = 0 (initially, but changes due to magnetic force on v_x)

For the speed to double:
Initial speed: v_0
Final speed: 2v_0

Velocity components:
v_x = a_x t = (qE_0/m)t
v_y = v_0 (remains constant as no force in y-direction from E field)

Final speed: V = sqrt(v_x^2 + v_y^2) = 2v_0
v_x^2 + v_y^2 = 4v_0^2
v_x^2 + v_0^2 = 4v_0^2
v_x^2 = 3v_0^2
v_x = sqrt(3)v_0

Since v_x = (qE_0/m)t:
sqrt(3)v_0 = (qE_0/m)t

t = (sqrt(3)mv_0)/(qE_0)

A.text: Mass per unit area of a circular disc of radius a depends on the distance r from its centre as σ(r) = A + Br. The moment of inertia of the disc about the axis perpendicular to the plane and passing through its centre is-
A.sol_text:
Consider a circular disc of radius a with mass per unit area σ(r) = A + Br.

Consider a thin ring element at distance r from the centre with thickness dr.

Area of ring element: dl = 2πr dr

Mass of ring element: dm = σ(r) × dl = (A + Br) × 2πr dr

Moment of inertia of ring element about the axis perpendicular to the plane and passing through the centre:
dI = r^2 dm = r^2 × (A + Br) × 2πr dr = 2πr^3(A + Br) dr

Total moment of inertia:
I = ∫dI = ∫₀^a 2πr^3(A + Br) dr

I = ∫₀^a 2πr^3 A dr + ∫₀^a 2πr^3 Br dr

I = 2πA ∫₀^a r^3 dr + 2πB ∫₀^a r^4 dr

I = 2πA [r^4/4]₀^a + 2πB [r^5/5]₀^a

I = 2πA(a^4/4) + 2πB(a^5/5)

I = 2πa^4(A/4) + 2πa^5(B/5)

I = 2πa^4(A/4 + aB/5)

A.text: A stationary observer receives sound from two identical tuning forks, one of which approaches and the other one recedes with the same speed (much less than the speed of sound). The observer hears 2 beats/sec. The oscillation frequency of each tuning fork is v0 = 1400 Hz and the velocity of sound in air is 350 m/s. The speed of each tuning fork is close to -
A.sol_text:
For the approaching tuning fork, using Doppler effect:
f1 = (c/(c - v))f0

For the receding tuning fork, using Doppler effect:
f2 = (c/(c + v))f0

Beat frequency = f1 - f2
= cf0(1/(c - v) - 1/(c + v))
= cf0((c + v - c + v)/((c - v)(c + v)))
= cf0(2v/(c^2 - v^2))

Since c >> v, we can approximate c^2 - v^2 ≈ c^2

Beat frequency = (2f0v)/c = 2

Substituting values:
(2 × 1400 × v)/350 = 2

(2800v)/350 = 2

8v = 2

v = 1/4 m/s

A.text: Two ideal Carnot engines operate in cascade (all heat given up by one engine is used by the other engine to produce work) between temperature, T1 and T2. The temperature of the hot reservoir of the first engine is T1 and the temperature of the cold reservoir of the second engine is T2. T is temperature of the sink of first engine which is also the source for the second engine. How is T related to T1 and T2, if both the engines perform equal amount of work?
A.sol_text:
For two Carnot engines operating in cascade with equal work output:

For first engine: Q1 (heat input at T1), Q2 (heat output at T)
For second engine: Q2 (heat input at T), Q3 (heat output at T2)

For ideal Carnot engine:
Q2/Q1 = T/T1 ........... (i)
Q3/Q1 = T2/T ........... (ii)
Q3/Q1 = T2/T1 ........... (iii)

Since work is same for both engines:
Q1 - Q2 = Q2 - Q3
⇒ Q1 + Q3 = 2*Q2

Dividing by Q1:
T1/T + T2/T = 2
⇒ (T1 + T2)/T = 2
⇒ T = (T1 + T2)/2

A.text: An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of 10 person, with the average mass of each person being 68 kg. The mass of the elevator itself is 920 kg and it moves with a constant speed of 3 m/s. The frictional force opposing the motion is 6000 N. If the elevator is moving up with its full capacity, the power delivered by the motor to the elevator (g = 10 m/s^2) must be at least :
A.sol_text:
Given:
- Maximum capacity: 10 persons
- Average mass per person: 68 kg
- Mass of elevator: 920 kg
- Constant speed: v = 3 m/s
- Frictional force: f = 6000 N
- g = 10 m/s^2

Total mass when elevator is full:
M_total = 10 × 68 + 920 = 680 + 920 = 1600 kg

Weight of system:
W = M_total × g = 1600 × 10 = 16000 N

Since the elevator moves with constant speed (a = 0), the net force is zero.
Therefore, tension T in the cable equals:
T = W + f = 16000 + 6000 = 22000 N

Power delivered by motor:
Power = T × v = 22000 × 3 = 66000 W

A.text: A planar loop of wire rotates in a uniform magnetic field. Initially, at t = 0, the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field. If it rotates with a period of 10s about an axis in its plane then the magnitude of induced emf will be maximum and minimum, respectively at -
A.sol_text:
Given: Period T = 10s, initially at t = 0 the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

The magnetic flux through the loop is:
phi = vector B · vector A = BA cos(omega*t)

where omega = 2*pi/T = 2*pi/10 = pi/5 rad/s

The induced emf is:
epsilon = -d(phi)/dt = BA*omega*sin(omega*t)

|epsilon| = BA*omega*sin(omega*t)

For maximum emf:
sin(omega*t) = 1
omega*t = pi/2
(pi/5)*t = pi/2
t = 2.5 s

For minimum emf:
sin(omega*t) = 0
omega*t = pi
(pi/5)*t = pi
t = 5 s

Therefore, epsilon_max occurs at t = 2.5 s and epsilon_min occurs at t = 5 s.

A.text: A mass of 10 kg is suspended by a rope of length 4m, from the ceiling. A force F is applied horizontally at the mid-point of the rope such that the top half of the rope makes an angle of 45° with the vertical. Then F equals : (Take g = 10 ms^(-2) and the rope to be massless)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Under an adiabatic process, the volume of an ideal gas gets doubled. Consequently the mean collision time between the gas molecule changes from tau_1 to tau_2. If C_p/C_v = gamma for this gas then a good estimate for tau_2/tau_1 is given by
A.sol_text:
For an adiabatic process:
TV^(gamma-1) = constant .... (ii)

Mean collision time is given by:
tau ∝ V/sqrt(T) .... (i)

From TV^(gamma-1) = constant:
T_1 V_1^(gamma-1) = T_2 V_2^(gamma-1)

Given V_2 = 2V_1
T_1 V_1^(gamma-1) = T_2 (2V_1)^(gamma-1)
T_1 V_1^(gamma-1) = T_2 2^(gamma-1) V_1^(gamma-1)
T_1 = T_2 2^(gamma-1)
T_2 = T_1/2^(gamma-1)

Since tau ∝ V/sqrt(T):
tau ∝ V^((1+gamma)/2)

Therefore:
tau_2/tau_1 = (V_2/V_1)^((1+gamma)/2) × (T_1/T_2)^(1/2)

Or more directly:
tau_2/tau_1 = (V_2)^((1+gamma)/2) / (V_1)^((1+gamma)/2) × (T_1)^(1/2) / (T_2)^(1/2)

Using tau ∝ V^((1+gamma)/2):
tau_2/tau_1 = (2V_1/V_1)^((1+gamma)/2) = (2)^((1+gamma)/2) = (1/2)^(-(1+gamma)/2)

However, using the adiabatic relation directly:
Since V increases by factor 2, T decreases, so tau ∝ V/sqrt(T)
tau_2/tau_1 = (2)^((gamma+1)/2)

B.text: The balancing length for a cell is 560 cm in a potentiometer experiment. When an external resistance of 10Ω is connected in parallel to the cell, the balancing length changes by 60 cm. If the internal resistance of the cell is N/10 Ω, where N is an integer then value of N is ................
B.sol_text:
From the potentiometer circuit diagram:

Initially (without external resistance):
E = 560x  ......(i)
where x is the potential gradient

With internal resistance r and balancing length 560 cm:
E - ir = 500x

After connecting 10Ω in parallel to the cell:
The equivalent resistance becomes: R_eq = (10 × r)/(10 + r)

Current through potentiometer: i' = E/(R_eq + R_0)

The new balancing length is 500 cm (changed by 60 cm from 560 cm)

Using potentiometer principle:
E = 560x  ......(i)

With 10Ω in parallel:
10E/(10 + r) = 500x  ......(ii)

Dividing (i) by (ii):
[560x × (10 + r)]/(10 + r × 500x) = 560/(500x) × (10 + r)/(10)

560(10 + r)/(10E) = 500x

560(10 + r) = 500x × 10E

560(10 + r) = 5000xE

From (i): E = 560x

560(10 + r) = 5000x × 560x

Simplifying the equations:
10E/(10 + r) = 500x

10 × 560x/(10 + r) = 500x

5600x/(10 + r) = 500x

5600/(10 + r) = 500

5600 = 500(10 + r)

5600 = 5000 + 500r

600 = 500r

r = 600/500 = 1.2 Ω

r = N/10 = 1.2

N = 12
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A 60 pF capacitor is fully charged by a 20 V supply. It is then disconnected from the supply and is connected to another uncharged 60pF capacitor in parallel. The electrostatic energy that is lost in this process by the time the charge is redistributed between them is (in nJ)
B.sol_text:
Initial state: First capacitor (C = 60 pF) is charged to V_0 = 20 V

Initial energy: E_i = (1/2)CV_0^2 = (1/2)(60 × 10^(-12))(20)^2 = (1/2)(60 × 10^(-12))(400) = 12 × 10^(-9) J = 12 nJ

When connected in parallel:
Both capacitors have same capacitance C = 60 pF
Total charge is conserved: Q_total = CV_0 = 60 × 10^(-12) × 20 = 1.2 × 10^(-9) C

Total capacitance in parallel: C_total = C + C = 120 pF

Final voltage across both capacitors: V_f = Q_total/C_total = (1.2 × 10^(-9))/(120 × 10^(-12)) = 10 V

Final energy: E_f = (1/2)C_total × V_f^2 = (1/2)(120 × 10^(-12))(10)^2 = (1/2)(120 × 10^(-12))(100) = 6 × 10^(-9) J = 6 nJ

Energy lost: ΔE = E_i - E_f = 12 - 6 = 6 nJ

Alternatively, using the formula:
ΔE = (1/2)CV_0^2 - 2[(1/2)C(V_0/2)^2] = (1/2)CV_0^2 - (1/4)CV_0^2 = (1/4)CV_0^2 = CV_0^2/4
= (60 × 10^(-12) × 400)/4 = 6 × 10^(-9) = 6 nJ
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The sum of two forces P and Q is R such that |R| = |P|. The angle theta (in degrees) that the resultant of 2P and Q will make with Q is, .............
B.sol_text:
Given: vector P + vector Q = vector R and |R| = |P|

From vector addition:
vector P + vector Q = vector R

Taking magnitude squared:
|P|^2 + |Q|^2 + 2|P||Q|cos(theta) = |R|^2 = |P|^2

Simplifying:
|Q|^2 + 2|P||Q|cos(theta) = 0
2|P|cos(theta) + |Q| = 0  ...(1)

For the resultant of 2P and Q, using tan(alpha) formula:
tan(alpha) = (2|P| sin(theta))/(2|P| cos(theta) + |Q|)  ...(2)

From equation (1): 2|P|cos(theta) + |Q| = 0

Substituting in equation (2):
tan(alpha) = (2|P| sin(theta))/0 = infinity

Therefore: alpha = 90°
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: M grams of steam at 100° C is mixed with 200 g of ice at its melting point in a thermally insulated container. If it produces liquid water at 40° C [heat of vaporization of water is 540 cal/g and heat of fusion of ice is 80 cal/g], the value of M is ............... .
B.sol_text:
M gm steam at 100° C + M gm ice at 0° C

Steam at 100° C:
Heat released = M × 540 cal
Converts to M gm water at 100° C

Ice at 0° C:
Heat required to melt = 200 × 80 = 16000 cal
Converts to 200 gm water at 0° C

Water from steam at 100° C:
Using MSAT = M × 1 × 60 = 60 M cal
This cools M gm water from 100° C to 40° C

Water from ice at 0° C:
Heat required = 200 × 1 × 40 = 8000 cal
This heats 200 gm water from 0° C to 40° C

Total heat released from steam = 600 M cal
Total heat required for ice and cooling = 24000 M cal

Energy balance:
600 M = 24000 M

Actually, heat released by steam condensing and cooling:
M × 540 (condensation) + M × 1 × 60 (cooling from 100° C to 40° C) = 600 M cal

Heat required by ice:
200 × 80 (melting) + 200 × 1 × 40 (warming from 0° C to 40° C) = 16000 + 8000 = 24000 cal

Setting heat released = heat required:
600 M = 24000

M = 40 gm
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

If the coefficient of friction is μ = 0.4, the maximum possible value of 100 x b/a for box not to topple before moving is ................. .

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Among the statements(a)-(d), the incorrect ones are: (a) Octahedral Co(III) complexes with strong field ligands have very high magnetic moments (b) When Δ_0 < P, the d-electron configuration of Co(III) in an octahedral complex is t_2g^6 e_g^2 (c) Wavelength of light absorbed by [Co(en)_3]^(3+) is lower than that of [CoF_6]^(3-) (d) If the Δ_0 for an octahedral complex of Co(III) is 18,000 cm^(-1), the Δ_t for its tetrahedral complex with the same ligand will be 16,000 cm^(-1)
A.sol_text: Strong field ligands have high pairing energy. For strong field ligand: Δ_0 = Δ_t × 1.125. 18000/1.125 = Δ_t, 16000 = Δ_t. (a) Octahedral Co(III) complexes with strong field ligands have t_2g^6 e_g^0 configuration (low spin), which gives very low magnetic moments (zero for Co(III) in octahedral geometry with strong field), so this statement is incorrect. (b) When Δ_0 < P (weak field), Co(III) would have high spin configuration t_2g^5 e_g^2 or similar, but the statement shows t_2g^6 e_g^2 which is not possible for Co(III) d^6 ion. Actually, when Δ_0 < P, Co(III) has high spin t_2g^4 e_g^2 configuration, not t_2g^6 e_g^2, so this statement is incorrect. (c) [Co(en)_3]^(3+) has en which is a stronger field ligand than F^-, so it absorbs light of higher energy (shorter wavelength). This statement is correct. (d) The calculation confirms Δ_t = 16,000 cm^(-1), which is correct. The incorrect statements are (a) and (d) is actually correct upon rechecking, so answer is (2): (a) and (d) only. However, reviewing (b) again - it appears to be the other incorrect statement along with (a).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: If the following reaction sequence, starting material is aniline with para-methyl group (4-methylaniline). First step: Ac2O/AcOH converts it to compound A (N-acetyl-4-methylaniline). Second step: Br2/AcOH converts A to compound B. What is the major product B?
options: N-acetyl compound with Br at ortho position relative to acetyl group and CH3 at para position
N-acetyl compound with both COCH3 and Br substituents on the benzene ring
N-acetyl compound with Br at ortho position relative to CH3 group (which becomes CH2Br)
N-acetyl compound with Br at meta position relative to acetyl group and CH3 at para position
A.sol_text:
Starting with 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine):

Step 1: Ac2O/AcOH → Compound A
The amino group (-NH2) undergoes acetylation to form N-acetyl-4-methylaniline (A), with structure: CH3-C6H4-NH-CO-CH3

Step 2: Br2/AcOH → Compound B
The acetamide group (-NHCOCH3) is a strong ortho/para-directing group (deactivating but directing) due to the NH being part of the amide.
The methyl group (-CH3) is also an ortho/para-directing group (activating).

Both groups direct incoming electrophiles to ortho and para positions. However, the acetamide group's directing effect is dominant. The bromine will preferentially enter at the ortho position relative to the acetamide group.

Given that there is already a methyl group at the para position relative to the acetamide, bromination occurs at the ortho position(s) to the acetamide group (which are meta to the methyl group).

The major product B is: N-acetyl-4-methylaniline with bromine at the position ortho to the acetamide group and meta to the methyl group.

This corresponds to the structure shown in option (4): NHCOCH3 group with Br at ortho position and CH3 at para position (meta relationship between Br and CH3).

A.text: Among statement (a) – (d), the correct ones are: (a) Decomposition of hydrogen peroxide gives dioxygen. (b) Like hydrogen peroxide, compound, such as KClO3, Pb(NO3)2 and NaNO3 when heated liberate dioxygen. (c) 2-Ethylanthraquinone is useful for the industrial preparation of hydrogen peroxide. A.text: The correct order of stability for the following alkoxides is: (A) Structure with O^(-) bonded to carbon with NO2 group and methyl group (B) Structure with O^(-) bonded to carbon with NO2 group and double bond to C (C) Structure with O^(-) bonded to carbon in conjugation with NO2 group through C=C double bond
A.sol_text:
To determine the stability of alkoxides, we need to analyze the factors that stabilize the negative charge on oxygen.

Structure (A): O^(-)-CH(NO2)-CH3
The negative charge is stabilized by the electron-withdrawing NO2 group attached directly to the carbon bearing the oxygen. This provides inductive stabilization.

Structure (B): O^(-)-C(=O)-NO2 (structure shows a resonance form)
The negative charge is stabilized by resonance with the NO2 group. The negative charge can be delocalized into the pi system, providing resonance stabilization.

Structure (C): O^(-)-CH=CH-NO2
The negative charge on the oxygen can be stabilized by: (1) Mesomeric effect of NO2 group through conjugation via C=C double bond, (2) The negative charge can delocalize through the extended conjugated system (O^(-) - C=C - NO2).

Order of stabilization:
- Structure (C) is most stable because the negative charge can be delocalized through the entire conjugated π-system (O^(-) - C=C - N(O)=O), providing maximum resonance stabilization through the extended conjugation.
- Structure (B) is next because it has resonance stabilization but through a more localized system.
- Structure (A) is least stable because it relies only on the inductive effect of the directly attached NO2 group.

Therefore, the stability order is: (C) > (B) > (A)

A.text: The locus of the mid-points of the perpendiculars drawn from points on the line, x = 2y to the line x = y is:
A.sol_text:
Let A(2a, a) be a point on the line x = 2y.
Let B(beta, beta) be a point on the line x = y.
Let M(h, k) be the mid-point of the perpendicular from A to B.

Since AB is perpendicular to the line x = y (which has slope 1), the slope of AB = -1.

Slope AB = (k - alpha)/(h - 2a) = -1
=> k - alpha = -(h - 2a)
=> k - alpha = -h + 2a
=> alpha = k + h - 2a ......(1)

Since M(h, k) is the mid-point of AB:
(2a + beta)/2 = h
(a + beta)/2 = k

From these:
beta + 2a = 2h
beta + a = 2k

Subtracting: a = 2h - 2k ......(2)

From (1) & (2):
alpha = k + h - 2(2h - 2k)
alpha = k + h - 4h + 4k
alpha = 5k - 3h

Also from beta + 2a = 2h and beta + a = 2k:
beta = 2h - 2a

Substituting a = 2h - 2k:
beta = 2h - 2(2h - 2k)
beta = 2h - 4h + 4k
beta = 4k - 2h

Since B(beta, beta) lies on x = y:
beta = beta (which is always true)

For the perpendicularity condition:
The slope of AB is -1, and slope of x = y is 1.
Slope AB = (beta - a)/(beta - 2a) = -1

(4k - 2h) - (2h - 2k) = -(4k - 2h - 2a)
6k - 4h = -(4k - 2h - 2(2h - 2k))
6k - 4h = -(4k - 2h - 4h + 4k)
6k - 4h = -(-6h + 8k)
6k - 4h = 6h - 8k
14k = 10h
5h = 7k
=> 5x = 7y

Therefore, the locus is 5x - 7y = 0

A.text: Let the tangents drawn from the origin to the circle, x^2 + y^2 - 8x - 4y + 16 = 0 touch it at the points A and B. The (AB)^2 is equal to:
A.sol_text:
First, rewrite the circle equation in standard form:
x^2 + y^2 - 8x - 4y + 16 = 0
(x^2 - 8x) + (y^2 - 4y) + 16 = 0
(x^2 - 8x + 16) + (y^2 - 4y + 4) + 16 - 16 - 4 = 0
(x - 4)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 4

Center C = (4, 2) and Radius R = 2

Distance from origin O(0,0) to center C(4,2):
OC = sqrt(4^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(16 + 4) = sqrt(20) = 2sqrt(5)

Let L denote the length of tangent from O to the circle:
L = sqrt(OC^2 - R^2) = sqrt(20 - 4) = sqrt(16) = 4

Since OA and OB are tangents from O to the circle:
- OA = OB = 4
- CA ⊥ OA and CB ⊥ OB (radius perpendicular to tangent)
- CA = CB = 2
- In right triangle OAC: OA^2 + CA^2 = OC^2 ✓ (16 + 4 = 20)

For finding AB, use the formula:
Length of AB = (2RL)/sqrt(L^2 + R^2)

where L = distance of center from origin along the chord AB direction.

Alternatively, in quadrilateral OACB:
- ∠OAC = ∠OBC = 90°
- OA = OB = 4, CA = CB = 2, OC = 2sqrt(5)

Using the formula for chord length when two tangents are drawn:
AB = (2 × R × L)/sqrt(L^2 + R^2) = (2 × 2 × 4)/sqrt(16 + 4) = 16/sqrt(20) = 16/(2sqrt(5)) = 8/sqrt(5)

Wait, using correct approach:
In triangle OAC: OA = 4, AC = 2, OC = 2sqrt(5)
Angle ∠AOC = cos^(-1)(OA/OC) = cos^(-1)(4/(2sqrt(5))) = cos^(-1)(2/sqrt(5))

Similarly ∠BOC = cos^(-1)(2/sqrt(5))

Using the formula: AB^2 = 2R^2(1 - cos(∠ACB))
where ∠ACB = 2π - 2∠OAC - 2∠OCA

Simpler approach using formula:
AB^2 = (2RL)^2/(L^2 + R^2) where L is length of tangent

AB^2 = (2 × 2 × 4)^2/(16 + 4) = (16)^2/20 = 256/20 = 64/5

A.text: The value of c in the Lagrange's mean value theorem for the function f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 8x + 11, when x ∈ [0, 1] is:
A.sol_text:
f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 8x + 11, x ∈ [0, 1]
Using LMVT
f'(c) = (f(1) - f(0))/(1 - 0)

First, find f(1) and f(0):
f(1) = 1 - 4 + 8 + 11 = 16
f(0) = 11

Find f'(x):
f'(x) = 3x^2 - 8x + 8

Applying LMVT:
3c^2 - 8c + 8 = (16 - 11)/(1 - 0)
3c^2 - 8c + 8 = 5
3c^2 - 8c + 3 = 0

Using quadratic formula:
c = (8 ± sqrt(64 - 36))/6
c = (8 ± sqrt(28))/6
c = (8 ± 2sqrt(7))/6
c = (4 ± sqrt(7))/3

Since c ∈ (0, 1), we check:
c = (4 - sqrt(7))/3 ∈ (0, 1)
c = (4 + sqrt(7))/3 > 1 (not valid)

Therefore, c = (4 - sqrt(7))/3

A.text: Let A, B, C and D be four non-empty sets. The contrapositive statement of "If A ⊆ B and B ⊆ D, then A ⊆ C" is:
options: If A ⊄ C, then A ⊆ B and B ⊆ D
If A ⊄ C, then A ⊄ B and B ⊆ D
If A ⊄ C, then A ⊄ B or B ⊄ D
If A ⊆ C, then B ⊂ A or D ⊂ B
A.sol_text:
If A ⊆ B and B ⊆ D then A ⊆ C

Contrapositive is
If A ⊄ C, then A ⊄ B or B ⊄ D

The contrapositive of a statement "If P then Q" is "If not Q then not P".

Here P = (A ⊆ B and B ⊆ D)
Q = A ⊆ C

Negation of Q: not (A ⊆ C) = A ⊄ C
Negation of P: not (A ⊆ B and B ⊆ D) = (A ⊄ B) or (B ⊄ D)

Therefore the contrapositive is:
If A ⊄ C, then A ⊄ B or B ⊄ D

A.text: In a workshop, there are five machines and the probability of any one of them to be out of service on a day is 1/4. If the probability that at most two machines will be out of service on the same day is (3/4)^3 * k, then k is equal to:
A.sol_text:
Prob. (at most two machines will be out of service) = (3/4)^3 * k

Using binomial distribution with n=5, p=1/4 (probability of being out of service), q=3/4 (probability of working):

P(X ≤ 2) = C(5,0)*(3/4)^5 + C(5,1)*(1/4)*(3/4)^4 + C(5,2)*(1/4)^2*(3/4)^3

= (3/4)^5 + 5*(1/4)*(3/4)^4 + 10*(1/4)^2*(3/4)^3

= (3/4)^3 * k

=> 17/8 * (3/4)^3 = (3/4)^3 * k

=> k = 17/8

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution curve of the differential equation, (y^2 - x) dy/dx = 1, satisfying y(0) = 1. This curve intersects the x-axis at a point whose abscissa is:
A.sol_text:
From the given differential equation (y^2 - x) dy/dx = 1

Rearranging: dx/dy = y^2 - x

This can be written as: dy/dx + x = y^2

This is a linear differential equation in x as a function of y.

Integrating factor: I.F. = e^(∫1 dy) = e^y

Multiplying both sides by e^y:
x.e^y = ∫y^2.e^y dy

Using integration by parts twice:
∫y^2.e^y dy = y^2.e^y - ∫2y.e^y dy
= y^2.e^y - 2y.e^y + ∫2.e^y dy
= y^2.e^y - 2y.e^y + 2e^y + C

Therefore: x.e^y = y^2.e^y - 2y.e^y + 2e^y + C

Applying initial condition y(0) = 1:
0.e^1 = 1.e^1 - 2(1).e^1 + 2e^1 + C
0 = e - 2e + 2e + C
0 = e + C
C = -e

So: x.e^y = y^2.e^y - 2y.e^y + 2e^y - e

The curve intersects the x-axis when y = 0:
x.e^0 = 0.e^0 - 2(0).e^0 + 2e^0 - e
x = 0 - 0 + 2 - e
x = 2 - e

B.text:
If the system of linear equations,
x + y + z = 6
x + 2y + 3z = 10
3x + 2y + lambda*z = mu
has more than two solutions, then mu - lambda^2 is equal to ________.
B.sol_text:
For the system to have more than two solutions (infinite solutions), the determinant of the coefficient matrix must be zero.

delta = |1  1  1|
        |1  2  3| = 0
        |3  2  lambda|

Expanding along the first row:
1(2*lambda - 3*2) - 1(1*lambda - 3*1) + 1(1*2 - 3*2) = 0
=> 1(2*lambda - 6) - 1(lambda - 9) + 1(-4) = 0
=> 2*lambda - 6 - lambda + 9 - 4 = 0
=> lambda - 1 = 0
=> lambda = 1

Now for infinite solutions, we also need:
delta_x = |6   1  1|
          |10  2  3| = 0
          |mu  2  lambda|

Expanding along the first row:
6(2*lambda - 3*2) - 1(10*lambda - 3*mu) + 1(10*2 - 2*mu) = 0
=> 6(2*lambda - 6) - 1(10*lambda - 3*mu) + 1(20 - 2*mu) = 0
=> 12*lambda - 36 - 10*lambda + 3*mu + 20 - 2*mu = 0
=> 2*lambda + mu - 16 = 0
=> 2(1) + mu - 16 = 0
=> 2 + mu = 16
=> mu = 14

Therefore:
mu - lambda^2 = 14 - 1^2 = 14 - 1 = 13
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: If the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point (1, 0, 3) on a line passing through (α, 7, 1) is (5/3, 7/3, 17/3), then α is equal to ________.
B.sol_text:
Let P = (1, 0, 3) be the given point
Let A = (α, 7, 1) be a point on the line
Let D = (5/3, 7/3, 17/3) be the foot of the perpendicular from P to the line

Since D is the foot of perpendicular from P to the line passing through A, we have:
vector PD ⊥ vector AD

Calculate vector PD:
vector PD = D - P = (5/3 - 1, 7/3 - 0, 17/3 - 3) = (2/3, 7/3, 8/3)

Calculate vector AD:
vector AD = D - A = (5/3 - α, 7/3 - 7, 17/3 - 1) = (5/3 - α, -14/3, 14/3)

For perpendicularity, vector PD · vector AD = 0:
((5/3 - α)i + (7/3 - 7)j + (17/3 - 1)k) · ((2/3)i + (7/3)j + (8/3)k) = 0

(5/3 - α)(2/3) + (7/3)(-14/3) + (14/3)(8/3) = 0

(5/3 - α)(2/3) + 7/3(-14/3) + 14 × 8/3 = 0

2(5 - 3α)/3 - 14 × 7/3 + 14 × 8/3 = 0

2(5 - 3α) - 14 × 7 + 14 × 8 = 0

10 - 6α - 98 + 112 = 0

5 - 3α - 49 + 56 = 0

3α = 12

α = 4
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
